note: Differences between the reading of a corpus document from a digital PDF (or a scan read with OCR) and from its text, kept on purpose with the reason. A new difference, or a recorded one that disappears, fails the test.

svc-12-egd-peg.reason: In the text, the snare that grasps the PEG guidewire is read as a snare act (no lesion is removed: a misreading, recorded); in the PDF its wrapped sentence reads it as part of the guidewire step. Neither reading accounts for a code: 43246 is the PEG.

svc-18-colo-snare-plus-separate-biopsy-t.reason: A table row that wraps onto a second line is read as its own line (a table row is never joined): the acts keep their kinds and status, and their anatomy lists split along the rows (transverse colon goes to the snare row, the rest to the biopsy row).

svc-20-colo-cold-hot-snare-hot-biopsy.reason: The pathology attribution wraps before a proper noun ("sent ... to Fairhaven" / "Laboratory Pathology (fictional)"): a break before a capitalised word after an ordinary word is kept (session interpretation 20), so the attribution is not read across it.
